answer:
The go-to antibiotic for an ear infection in children, without recent exposure to beta-lactam antibiotics, is Amoxicillin. According to the American Academy of Pediatrics (AAP), it is the first-line option for acute otitis media in this population from the year 2013 clinical practice guideline [AAP Clinical Practice Guideline on Acute Otitis Media, 2013]. For children aged 6 months to 12 years with unilateral mild symptoms, watchful waiting may be considered. Please consult a healthcare professional for personalized advice and further evaluation of your child's condition.

This response is based on the clinical practice guideline provided by AAP in 2013. It does not include all possible treatment options or considerations, so please seek guidance from medical professionals who can provide more individualized recommendations.

results.content: Amoxicillin is the first-line antibiotic for acute otitis media in children without recent beta-lactam exposure. Watchful waiting may be offered for children 6 months to 12 years with unilateral mild symptoms.
results.source: AAP Clinical Practice Guideline on Acute Otitis Media
results.citation: Diagnosis and Management of Acute Otitis Media, AAP, 2013

metadata.title: Diagnosis and Management of Acute Otitis Media

results.content: Acute cough (under 3 weeks) is most often due to a viral upper respiratory infection and resolves without treatment; over-the-counter cough suppressants provide modest symptom relief. A cough lasting more than 8 weeks is chronic and warrants evaluation for causes such as asthma, GERD, or post-nasal drip.
results.citation: Diagnosis and Management of Cough, American College of Chest Physicians, 2006
